prompt: A discrete random variable $X$ takes the values $0, 1, 2, 3$ with $P(0) = 0.15$, $P(1) = 0.35$, $P(2) = \,?$, and $P(3) = 0.10$. What is $P(X = 2)$?
hint: The probabilities in a valid distribution must add up to exactly $1$.

hints.text: The probabilities in a valid distribution must add up to exactly $1$.
Add the three known probabilities and subtract from $1$.

explanation: A probability distribution lists every possible outcome, so its probabilities sum to $1$.
The missing one fills the gap: $1 - 0.60 = 0.40$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in percents
steps: The known outcomes cover $15\% + 35\% + 10\% = 60\%$ of all cases.
The other $40\%$ of cases must be $X = 2$.
